question: What incentives exist for commercial solar in Massachusetts?
html:
Our current research does not cover Massachusetts solar incentive programs, so we can't list them reliably here. Below is where solar fits in our work and the data that would answer the question properly.

What our research covers

  • Solar in the growth plan. Solar and storage O&M is one of the Phase 3 recurring-service lines. These lines are meant to turn one-off bids into ongoing contracts (CET growth plan).
  • Recent Massachusetts solar-adjacent work. The Massport Worcester Regional Airport 149A trade-contractor RFQ included electrical, fire alarm, lighting and "renewable energy upgrades." It was due Oct 8, 2026 (CET opportunity radar).
  • Massachusetts pipeline depth. The radar tracks 25 Massachusetts items. Automated access to several state sources was blocked, so parts of the Massachusetts list are incomplete (CET opportunity radar).

What our research lacks

TopicIn our data?What would answer it
State solar incentive programsNoCurrent program rules and capacity from the state energy agency
Federal tax credits for commercial solarNoCurrent federal guidance, reviewed by tax advisors
Utility rebates and interconnectionNoUtility tariff and program pages for the service territories we work in
Solar project bids in MassachusettsPartialHand-pulled COMMBUYS listings, since automated access was blocked

We have no incentive dollar amounts, eligibility terms or deadlines on file. We won't estimate them. Customers should confirm program details with the administering agency or their own advisors. This is not legal, tax or compliance advice.

How we can help today

  • Electrical construction and upgrades on commercial sites, including renewable-energy scopes like the Worcester airport package.
  • Efficiency work through NuWave, which the growth plan pairs with solar and storage O&M as recurring service.
  • Coverage across six New England states under existing licensing (CET growth plan).

Incentive terms shape whether a customer's solar project gets built, and that determines whether the solar and storage O&M line can reach the roughly 25% recurring service mix the growth plan targets by month 36 (est.).

Next actions

  1. Assign one estimator to build a short brief on Massachusetts and federal commercial solar incentives, sourced from agency pages and reviewed by tax counsel before it reaches customers.
  2. Pull COMMBUYS solar and renewable listings by hand, since automated access was blocked, and add them to the opportunity radar.
  3. Confirm the outcome of the Worcester airport 149A RFQ (due Oct 8, 2026) and note whether the renewable scope was awarded separately.
  4. Ask NuWave which of its current customers have solar or storage on site, as a starting list for O&M service contracts.
